newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Philip Morris trades up.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Philip Morris trades up.

text.p: Tobacco company Philip Morris Cos Inc was trading at 44 in the after-hours session compared to a close of 43-3/4 on the New York Stock Exchange following a Florida jury ruling, dealers said Monday.
"Philip is what's hot today," said one trader, referring to the amount of trading that it was getting.
The company's stock price rose after a jury ruled that R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co was not negligent in the death of a former smoker.
RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, of which Reynolds is a unit, was trading at 32-3/4 against a close of 32-5/8.
The exchange resumed trading in Philip Morris just before the end of normal trading hours. It had halted it earlier in the day in anticipation of the jury ruling in Jacksonville, Florida.
It resumed trading in Reynolds and Nabisco after the bell.
Another dealer said Nabisco had not yet traded during the after-hours session.

Genzyme Corp was trading at 20 against a Nasdaq close of 22-5/16. Its stock resumed trading after a Food and Drug Administration panel voted against granting the company approval for a coating solution.
The NYSE withheld America Online Inc from trading after the company released its third-quarter results, reporting a profit of $0.02 a share against $0.14 for the same period a year ago.
Also, the exchange said session one had a volume of 13,900 shares, compared with 6,400 on Friday. Session two had 245,400 against 1.2 million the previous trading day, it said.
